3) Target $/1M tokens you're comfortable with for planning (ballpark is fine).

- A regional pricing summary (US vs EU) with examples for 1M and 50M tokens, and notes on reserved/dedicated options that reduce unit cost.

Thanks Sophie — helpful detail. Quick pricing summary and illustrative unit economics (high level):

Assumptions: hosted API (no private control plane), using a high-capability open model variant we recommend for chat. Numbers rounded for planning.

1) Hosted (pay-as-you-go) — rough list-range per 1M tokens:
   - US region: $120–$160 / 1M tokens (varies by model variant & compute intensity)
   - EU region: typically +15% due to regional infra and capacity costs => $138–$184 / 1M tokens

2) Dedicated / Reserved capacity (monthly commit, 6–12m contracts) — approximate blended unit costs at scale:
   - 50M tokens/mo commit: $60–$95 / 1M tokens (US baseline)
   - EU-resident dedicated pool: adds ~10–20% delta => $66–$114 / 1M tokens

3) Private (on-prem / VPC) — higher fixed infra & support fees; unit cost can be competitive at very large scale but typically requires a platform fee + infra OPEX.

Example unit-economics illustrations (for planning):
- 1M tokens (single month, hosted): US ~$140; EU ~$160 (midpoint)
- 50M tokens (dedicated commit, blended): US ~$80/1M => $4,000/mo; EU blend ~$92/1M => $4,600/mo

Notes and levers that affect these numbers:
- Model variant: larger models increase cost per token; we can recommend variants that meet quality needs while controlling unit cost.
- Batching/prefix caching: for summarization/long-context flows, caching reduces billable tokens and effective cost.
- Commitment length and volume: committed reserved capacity yields the biggest delta.
- EU-only residency requires dedicated EU capacity in many cases; that is the main driver of the regional delta.

I've attached a short pricing_matrix.csv and a one-pager that outlines the math per 1M/10M/50M tokens. Bring any specific volume scenarios to the workshop and Marcus can run contract-level models.

Proposed times: Wed 11/19 10–11am PT (matches your slot). If that works I'll send a calendar invite and include the pricing materials + a short agenda.

Attachments: pricing_matrix.csv

Cheers,

Sophie — quick technical notes to add context for the workshop: 

- For the assistant flows, token consumption depends heavily on prompt strategy. If you can share a couple of representative prompts we can quantify expected billable tokens and show caching benefits.
- Embeddings/similarity lookups: these are usually cheaper per request than chat tokens but storage and retrieval cost should be included in the model.
- Reserved capacity: aside from unit-price discounts, reserved pools reduce inter-region transfer costs if we pin EU traffic to an EU-only pool. That is why dedicated capacity reduces the regional delta.
- Quantization / runtime optimizations: for latency-sensitive calls we can recommend quantized model variants that keep quality high but reduce compute cost; these can drop effective token cost vs a non-quantized baseline.

I've uploaded a short regional_pricing_breakdown.pdf (attached) that illustrates the EU-hosted capacity sizing and where the +15%–20% delta comes from (reserved GPU availability + higher infra unit costs + data residency routing). Happy to walk through the PDF in the workshop.

-Vivek
